title: amico skill frontmatter
description: The SKILL.md frontmatter contract (amicode#996): codifies exactly what the extension's skill loader enforces today — a required non-empty name + description — plus typed optional fields the loader or the revision resolver reads (surface, entitlement, revision, source, agents). Deliberately LENIENT on the passthrough extras (scenarios, vault_contract, project_contract, public_refs, provides_helpers) and the opencode-native passthroughs (stub, cli_tool, argument-hint, disable-model-invocation): additionalProperties stays open so the schema never blocks a legitimate extension. The entitlement pairing is enforced here because it is a property of the frontmatter alone: surface: entitled REQUIRES a non-empty entitlement code, and an entitlement code on anything else is flagged. NOT filename-kinded (SKILL.md frontmatter, validated as a parsed object); excluded from the version map — the library-paper precedent for frontmatter-shaped kinds.

name.description: the skill's identity — must equal its folder name (a structural rule the verb checks; the schema types the field)

description.description: the one-line summary the loader requires and the index renders

surface.description: the least-privilege staging tag (spec-20260713-003804): public ships and loads for all; entitled ships but stages only behind its entitlement code; internal never ships. Optional — internal and minimal skills without it must validate.

entitlement.description: the code a session must hold for a surface: entitled skill to stage (ADR-0011); meaningful only paired with surface: entitled

revision.description: the typed revision contract (spec-20260905-063000 D2): a monotonic non-negative integer, missing = 0

source.description: the copy's source label (the revision resolver's provenance field)

agents.description: the agent roles the skill targets; may be empty (the loader ignores it, opencode tolerates it)

allOf.$comment: surface: entitled REQUIRES a non-empty entitlement code — an entitled skill without a code can never stage from any root (the loader drops it). Emptiness is caught by entitlement's own minLength 1.
the converse pairing: an entitlement code on a non-entitled (or untagged) skill is flagged — the code would be dead weight the loaders never read.
